result.summary: TASK-002 executed: overrides.sharp raised from ^0.35.0 to ^0.35.4, making the sharp security floor declared rather than coincidental. One line of apps/web/package.json; 0 packages added, removed or version-changed in the lockfile.
unexpectedFindings: The lockfile reconciliation also drops a stale dev:true flag on fsevents. A control test on the UNMODIFIED package.json removes the same flag, so it is pre-existing drift inherited from PR 48 rather than a consequence of this change. Kept rather than reverted, because reverting would leave the committed lockfile disagreeing with npm deterministic output.

npx prettier --check on the edited package.json fails, and it is not a defect: the working-tree file is CRLF under core.autocrlf while the LF content git commits is clean. This falsified the checking rule EVC-023 addendum 1 had just established, and addendum 2 corrects it to read the file out of the index rather than off disk.

RISK-002 is narrower than it reads. The other four overrides entries share the structural property that made sharp dangerous - a declared floor below the resolved version - but none carries a current production advisory, so none is a vulnerability today.
scopeDeviations: docs/EVIDENCE_CONFLICTS.md was edited during this session and is outside TASK-002 allowed scope. scope-check refused it, correctly. The governance findings were moved into their own commit c455593 so the task commit stays within scope; the file is not attributed to this session.

The approval records in sdd.json and spec.md were written before the session was opened and are reported by scope-check as pre-existing and unattributed, which is accurate - they are the human gate records, not task work.
newUnknowns: Whether npm will reintroduce the fsevents dev flag on a future reconcile under a different Node or npm version. The control test fixes the behaviour for this toolchain only.
Whether any other committed lockfile metadata is similarly stale. Only the fsevents flag surfaced here because only it changed; nothing systematically checked the rest.
